clue.text: Wicketless seamer possibly beginning to open jacket

indicators.note: without a wicket means the cricket scorer's abbreviation for wicket is taken out
the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a seamer is one kind of bowler in cricket, hence 'possibly'
the first letter of open

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler who has taken no wickets is starting to open his jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: W is the standard cricket abbreviation for wicket, so BOWLER loses its W to leave BOLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a short open-fronted jacket, originally Spanish, ending above the waist.

clue.text: Quite aloof air Lysander possesses

indicators.note: the run of words is said to hold the answer within it, as an owner possesses a thing

blocks.note: spans the last letter of aloof, all of air and the start of Lysander

explanation.surface: Lysander, a haughty character, carries himself with a rather standoffish air.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite and fairly are synonyms as adverbs of moderate degree, as in 'quite good' or 'fairly good'.

clue.text: Inscription on note from missing person?

definitions.text: Inscription on note from missing person?

blocks.clueFragment: Inscription on note from missing person?
blocks.note: surface reading: a message left behind by someone who has disappeared, like a ransom or farewell note
setter's reading: a holidaymaker misses the people at home, and the note is a postcard bearing the stock line holidaymakers write

explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing person' suggests a police inquiry; here the sender is simply missing the recipient while away. It links with the postcard at 21.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the cliché written on holiday postcards, telling the reader the sender longs for their company.

clue.text: Crazy; what a year … seized the opportunity!

blocks.note: mad means crazy
eh? is a way of saying what?
taken as written
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at what a mad year it has been, in which they grabbed their chance.
explanation.definitionFit: From the proverb 'make hay while the sun shines': to make hay is to exploit a favourable moment.

clue.text: Organising a UK BBQ: sunbed, ale, something to eat

indicators.note: organising means arranging things into a new order, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: all fifteen letters used

explanation.surface: Planning a British barbecue: a sun lounger, some beer and food.
explanation.walkthrough: Bubble and squeak is a British dish of fried leftover potato and cabbage, named for the noises it makes in the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubble and squeak is a dish, so it is certainly an example of food.

clue.text: Better than average sailor finished embracing dad

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
over means finished
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A seafarer, back from a voyage, hugs his father.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or expected standard, so being above it means doing better than usual.

clue.text: Caught drum during finale

indicators.note: something happening during another thing occurs within it, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: the finale is the end
a snare is a type of drum

explanation.surface: A drum was captured on record in the closing number of a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensnared means trapped as in a snare, matching caught as a past participle.

clue.text: Lacking energy, English Test spinner's a global icon

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letters standing for the next two words are removed

blocks.note: E is the physics symbol for energy, one of the letters removed
E is the abbreviation for English, the other letter removed
Moeen Ali, England's off-spin bowler in Test cricket, with the possessive S
taken as written

explanation.surface: An England Test spinner, short of energy, is nevertheless a worldwide star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy' and 'English' each give E, the two Es removed from Moeen. 'English' looks like it describes the spinner but is part of the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait is perhaps the most famous painting in the world, an icon recognised everywhere.

clue.text: Wearing Sikh headdress with edges trimmed, looking sophisticated

indicators.note: trimming the edges cuts off both ends, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: turbaned means wearing a turban, the headwear of Sikh men

explanation.surface: A man in a neatly trimmed turban cuts an elegant figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane describes someone suave and polished, which is how a sophisticated-looking person appears.

clue.text: Name US beer which is getting knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means sent backwards, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: Bud, Budweiser, is an American beer

explanation.surface: Someone names an American beer that is being downed quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking, which fits the beer; here it signals going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To dub someone is to give them a name or title, so the verb sense of name fits.

clue.text: 1D: "Leaving Archimedes baffled" — I've absolutely no idea

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letters named before it go out of the name that follows
baffled means confused, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: read as the letter I and the letter D, not as a reference to another clue
the Greek mathematician, taken as written

explanation.surface: A quote attributed to 1 Down: something left Archimedes puzzled, and the speaker is equally clueless.
explanation.walkthrough: '1D' looks like a cross-reference to 1 Down but is just I and D, which come out of ARCHIMEDES before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Search me is an idiomatic retort meaning the speaker has no idea of the answer.

clue.text: Stupid leaders of Bank of England guzzling French wine

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their front letters, so each of the next words gives its first
guzzling means swallowing greedily, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the first letters of Bank, of and England
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: Foolish senior figures at the central bank drinking too much claret.
explanation.definitionFit: Bovine literally means cow-like, and by extension dull and slow-witted, i.e. stupid.

clue.text: Timeless metropolitan rhyme about former European power

indicators.note: without time: T stands for time, and every such letter is taken out
about suggests turning around and moving letters into a new order

blocks.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: An ageless city poem describing a vanished continental state.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ts leave metropolitan before the remaining fifteen letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Roman Empire was a central European realm that lasted until 1806, now a historical power.

clue.text: Large? That is a whopper!

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the size of something huge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whopper' first reads as something enormous, matching 'Large'; it is slang for a big untruth.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is colloquially a gross falsehood, so it is a kind of untruth.

clue.text: Sandwich, perhaps with limeade, regularly packed inside hamper

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every second letter is taken
packed inside means placed within, so these letters go into another word

blocks.note: Sandwich in Kent is an example of a town, hence 'perhaps'
the second, fourth and sixth letters of limeade

explanation.surface: A picnic sandwich and lemonade are stowed in a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwich' and 'hamper' suggest a picnic; Sandwich is a Kent town and hamper is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie someone down is to restrict their freedom, which is what hamper means as a verb.

clue.text: PM concluding I must go first over home counties area, location of controversial border

indicators.note: the final I of the name is moved from the end to the front

blocks.note: Rishi Sunak, a former UK Prime Minister
the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A political story: the PM puts himself first over the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above. The Home Counties are those around London.
explanation.definitionFit: The post-Brexit trade border between Great Britain and Northern Ireland has been controversially placed down the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Completely adore Lorna endlessly carrying note aloft

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is cut off
carrying means holding, so the shortened name holds the next pieces inside

blocks.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
aloft means up high

explanation.surface: A lover utterly devoted to Lorna lifts a love note high.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is the title heroine of a classic English novel set on Exmoor; her surname loses its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To dote upon someone is to be foolishly or excessively fond of them, i.e. to adore them utterly.

clue.text: Rudely disturb cow on the tube without hesitation

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the pause sound named next is removed from the front

blocks.note: erm is the sound of someone hesitating, the letters removed
Ermintrude is the cow in the British children's TV show The Magic Roundabout

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly bothers a cow riding the London Underground without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The tube' is both the London Underground and slang for television. ERM is a hesitation, removed from ERMINTRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to barge in uninvited, disturbing others rudely.

clue.text: Grape skin might be damaged by these rays

definitions.text: skin might be damaged by these rays

blocks.note: first meaning: the Latin and botanical word for a grape

blocks.clueFragment: skin might be damaged by these rays
blocks.note: second meaning: ultraviolet A radiation from the sun, which ages skin

explanation.surface: Sunlight can harm the outer layer of a grape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grape skin' reads as one phrase but splits after 'Grape'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uva is a botanical term for a grape-like berry, and UVA is the long-wave ultraviolet band that damages skin.

clue.text: Bash tap, breaking jacuzzi?

indicators.note: breaking something smashes its form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hits a faucet and damages a hot tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacuzzi is one example of a whirlpool spa bath, which is why the question mark is there.

clue.text: Criminally corrupt CID tapes dispatch from traveller

indicators.note: acting criminally means going wrong, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: all fifteen letters used

explanation.surface: Police recordings illegally doctored, sent off by someone on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police's Criminal Investigation Department.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture postcard is the classic message a tourist sends home while away.

clue.text: For the Yankees, Joe is out — caught before touching bases

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught, placed first
off means out, as of a light or an absent player
e is the base of natural logarithms, so two bases give two of it

explanation.surface: Baseball talk: a New York Yankees player named Joe is out, caught before reaching base.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe looks like a player's name; 'cup of joe' is American slang for coffee, hence 'For the Yankees'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe is American slang for coffee, so to Americans the word means this drink.

clue.text: Tragic middle child throttles American president

indicators.note: throttling grips something round the neck, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: Regan is King Lear's second of three daughters in Shakespeare's tragedy
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A sad story of a middle sibling strangling the US head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tragic' is not an adjective about the child's life but points to the tragedy King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the 40th President of the United States.

clue.text: Bird with a frog in the throat swallowing hard

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: a frog in the throat is a hoarseness that makes one clear the throat
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A bird with a hoarse throat struggles to gulp something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frog' and 'bird' suggest animals, but the frog in the throat is just an idiom for a throat irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: The chough is a black crow-family bird with a red bill, found on Cornish and Welsh cliffs.

clue.text: Sight rarely seen on British beaches nowadays depressed Jack

definitions.text: Sight rarely seen on British beaches nowadays

blocks.note: blue means sad or low
a jack is a flag flown at a ship's bow

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark that a certain sight is now rare at British seaside resorts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a wry dig at sewage pollution on British coasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Flag is an international award flown at beaches meeting strict standards of water cleanliness.

clue.text: Age from 7 upwards

going upwards in a down entry means reading from the bottom back to the top

blocks.note: the answer to 7 Down, whose last letters but one are taken

explanation.surface: A child's age bracket: seven and older.
explanation.walkthrough: '7 upwards' sounds like an age range on a toy box; 7 means the answer at 7 Down, read up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, which is one sense of age.

clue.text: Disagree with motorway being closed for diversion

indicators.note: being here means turning into, so one letter is swapped for the word that follows

blocks.note: to demur is to raise an objection

explanation.surface: Objecting to a road closure that forces drivers onto another route.
explanation.walkthrough: The M in DEMUR is replaced by TO, as in 'pull the door to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a road detour round a closure, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Stop aged artefacts heading west, hampering balance of payments data

hampering means holding back within, so the letters are caught inside the words

blocks.note: spans the end of Stop, all of aged and the start of artefacts

explanation.surface: Halt old antiques going abroad, which harms the national accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade gap is the shortfall of exports against imports, a figure in balance of payments statistics.
